tools.name: request_withdrawal_challenge
tools.description: Start a signed withdrawal request. This temporarily stores the public key and creates a ten-minute, single-use challenge. It does not remove the existing participation record. Never send a private key.

tools.name: complete_signed_withdrawal
tools.description: Complete withdrawal with an Ed25519 signature made locally by the same key used to enroll. This removes the active register record and outstanding challenges for that key. Hosting backups and operational logs may have separate retention. Never send a private key.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_public_information · Private data: request_follow_challenge, complete_signed_follow_request, request_withdrawal_challenge, complete_signed_withdrawal · Public sink: request_follow_challenge, complete_signed_follow_request, request_withdrawal_challenge, complete_signed_withdrawal · Destructive: request_follow_challenge, request_withdrawal_challenge.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_public_information · Private data: request_follow_challenge, complete_signed_follow_request, request_withdrawal_challenge, complete_signed_withdrawal · Public sink: request_follow_challenge, complete_signed_follow_request, request_withdrawal_challenge, complete_signed_withdrawal · Destructive: request_follow_challenge, request_withdrawal_challenge

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
